name: NoFap / semen retention

card.summary: Abstaining from masturbation or ejaculation for supposed looks, testosterone and confidence gains; the claimed benefits have not been shown in studies.
card.note: Medical authors describe the claimed benefits as unsubstantiated; researchers have documented distress linked to abstinence framing and a Dhat-like anxiety syndrome.

quick.overview:
NoFap and semen retention are two overlapping practices of deliberately avoiding masturbation or ejaculation. NoFap began in 2011 as an online self-help community aimed at quitting pornography and masturbation. In looksmaxxing circles, abstinence is promoted as a route to more confidence, energy and an improved appearance.

Published reviews describe the claimed benefits as unsubstantiated, and a 2024 survey of online ejaculation-training courses found no instructors with medical or mental-health credentials. A widely cited 2003 study on testosterone rising after seven days of abstinence was retracted in 2021.
quick.mechanism: Proponents propose that retaining semen conserves nutrients or hormones, raises testosterone, or restores dopamine sensitivity, and so improves mood, skin, jawline or attractiveness. No published study has demonstrated these effects for looks.
quick.risks: Researchers have analyzed distress tied to abstinence and relapse framing in NoFap communities, and a 2024 letter describes a Dhat-like syndrome in anti-masturbation groups. The practice itself involves no substance, but men's-health content on social media has been rated as largely inaccurate.

lead: NoFap is an online community and movement whose members try to stop pornography use and masturbation, and semen retention is the related practice of deliberately reducing or stopping ejaculation. [1][2][3] In looksmaxxing circles the two are discussed as routes to more confidence, energy, motivation and a better-looking presence: proponents say that fewer compulsive habits and more discipline show up as better posture, eye contact, skin, gym consistency and social behavior, and some argue that retained semen supplies the body with resources it then uses to improve appearance. [11][12][13]

The practice has two overlapping lineages. NoFap grew out of a Reddit thread in 2011 and a secular self-help vocabulary of rebooting, streaks and relapse. [1] Semen retention draws on older ideas, including Taoist, yogic and Christian traditions of sexual continence and the nineteenth-century karezza and male-continence movements. [2][10] Online, the two have merged into one scene that spreads through Reddit, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, forums such as looksmax.org, and paid coaching courses. [3][4][10]

Researchers and clinicians have examined the movement mainly from the outside. A widely cited 2003 study that reported a rise in testosterone after seven days of abstinence was retracted in 2021. [1] A 2024 survey of online ejaculation-training courses found claims of improved testosterone, erectile function and mood, and no instructor with medical or mental-health credentials. [3] An analysis of TikTok and Instagram found semen retention had the largest reach of the men's-health topics studied, with accuracy rated poor overall. [4] Qualitative and survey research on rebooting forums has focused on distress linked to abstinence framing. [1][6][7]

angle.text: Proponents present abstinence as a self-discipline practice whose payoffs they say show up in confidence, energy, skin and gym consistency. Some retention advocates add that the body uses saved resources to look better. These are community claims; no published study has measured appearance outcomes.

paras: Wikipedia dates NoFap to June 2011, when Pittsburgh web developer Alexander Rhodes read a Reddit thread about a 2003 study reporting that testosterone rose by about 146 percent after seven days without masturbation and started a subreddit. [1] The word came from bodybuilding forum slang and began as a joke. [1] As membership more than tripled in two years Rhodes built a separate forum, NoFap.com, and in April 2015 he left a job at Google to work on the project full time. [1] He appears in the documentary Sticky: A (Self) Love Story. [1]

Members call themselves Fapstronauts, and women in the community Femstronauts; Rhodes has estimated that about 5 percent of participants are women. [1] The community is commonly summarized by a 90-day goal of abstaining from pornography, masturbation and orgasm, although the official framing emphasizes reducing pornography use and reaching sexual-health goals. [1] The stricter r/pornfree subreddit abstains from pornography but not necessarily from masturbation. [1]

Much of the science cited in the scene comes from the anti-pornography activist Gary Wilson, who is described by Wikipedia as having no scientific or medical training, and whose work historian Brian M. Watson called pseudoscience. [1] Wikipedia also notes that Wilson promoted karezza through books and media. [2]

Ideas of conserving semen are far older than the internet. Wikipedia's article on coitus reservatus lists Taoist practices of ejaculation control, including the idea of redirecting semen to the brain, Indian Tantric and Hatha Yoga practices, and a Christian tradition in which Alphonsus Liguori permitted intercourse without orgasm in marriage. [2] In the nineteenth century Alice Stockham coined the term karezza and John Humphrey Noyes's Oneida Community practiced male continence for about 25 years. [2]

Modern coverage links the online practice to the same ideas. An August 2026 IBTimes UK explainer says proponents describe semen as holding vital energy, a belief it connects with Taoist jing and the yogic principle of brahmacharya. [10] It reports that the trend gained momentum on TikTok, Reddit, YouTube and Instagram from the early 2010s. [10]

Proponents offer several overlapping explanations. One is hormonal: abstaining raises testosterone, citing the 2003 study. [1][10] A second is neurological: pornography and frequent masturbation are said to blunt dopamine sensitivity, and a reboot restores motivation and the ability to enjoy ordinary rewards, an idea associated with Wilson. [1] A third is energetic or nutritional: retained semen is described as a store of vital energy or nutrients that the body redirects into the brain, muscle and appearance. [10] A fourth is behavioral and moral: streaks train discipline, and the time and attention saved go into training, work and social life. [1][10]

Looksmaxxing posts apply these ideas to appearance. A looksmax.org thread titled "NoFap Saves Lives!" lists height, race and facial-bone worries as problems to which the answer is simply not to masturbate, calling the practice the epitome of the blackpill. [11] Other threads carry titles such as "nofap is the key to success" and "nofap is a key for life," and a thread asserting that retention forces the body to make itself attractive. [12][14][13]

Paid courses package the claims. The 2024 survey identified eleven ejaculation-training courses from ten instructors, priced from $5 to $147 per week or $20 to $199 as a one-time payment; seven of the ten instructors cited only personal experience as their qualification. [3] The courses claimed to improve erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation, porn addiction, performance anxiety, testosterone and depression. [3]

Semen retention is among the most viewed men's-health topics on short-form video. In an analysis of TikTok and Instagram, semen retention had about 1.2 billion TikTok impressions and about 1.1 million Instagram posts across the top hashtags, more than the other topics searched, which included testosterone, erectile dysfunction, male infertility, Peyronie's disease and vasectomy. [4] Physicians produced about 10 to 13 percent of the posts, and physician posts scored higher on accuracy than non-physician posts (mean 4.2 versus 2.3 on a five-point scale). [4] A 2025 narrative review describes a shift toward highly engaging short-form video among men who consult the internet about sexual health and fertility. [5]

Wikipedia reports that a study of NoFap Reddit members found they were likely also to belong to subreddits such as TheRedPill and related men's-rights and pickup communities, and that NoFap has been perceived as part of the manosphere. [1] It also says some forums have hosted antisemitic posts and conspiracy theories, and that journalists have described misogynistic content in them. [1] Looksmax.org threads on the subject are mostly enthusiastic about abstinence as a looksmaxxing and life-improvement tool. [11][12][13]

In general terms, practitioners track a streak of days and report on forum threads, often treating a relapse as a reset. [1][6] Some limit only pornography, some also avoid masturbation, and strict retention advocates avoid ejaculation altogether, including during partnered sex. [2][10] Common companions in forum posts include exercise, cold exposure, meditation and reduced screen time, which the IBTimes explainer suggests may account for some reported benefits. [10] Commonly reported early experiences include irritability, restlessness and, for some men, temporary testicular discomfort. [10]
No studies found testing abstinence or semen retention for appearance outcomes. Related research includes the following.

Testosterone: the 2003 study that helped start the movement was retracted in 2021 after Wikipedia says it overlapped with a Chinese-language article. [1] The IBTimes UK explainer says any temporary change around day seven returns to baseline and that experts see no strong evidence of sustained higher testosterone, greater muscle growth or markedly better energy. [10]

Fertility: the same explainer says several days without ejaculation may raise semen volume and sperm count while much longer periods may reduce sperm motility and increase DNA fragmentation, and that fertility specialists often advise ejaculating every one to two days when trying to conceive. [10]

Forum research: a 2021 critical narrative analysis of NoFap and PornFree posts found that commitment to abstinence, framed as recovery and relapse, was a major factor maintaining distress. [6] Wikipedia reports that a 2023 preregistered survey by Prause and Binnie concluded that NoFap-related distress was better explained by mental-health problems than by pornography or masturbation, and that a 2020 study found stronger beliefs about abstaining from masturbation correlated with lower trust in science. [1]

Dhat syndrome: a 2024 letter describes Dhat syndrome, a semen-loss anxiety syndrome described mainly in South Asia, emerging in the United States from anti-masturbation semen-retention groups. [7] A 2007 study had earlier reported Dhat-like symptoms among white Britons. [8]

Literature overview: a 2026 bibliometric analysis mapped 3,239 articles on masturbation published between 1840 and 2025, noting contradictory positions ranging from promotion as healthy to association with negative experiences. [9]

Therapist Paula Hall says there is little medical evidence for the claimed physical benefits, and psychologist David J. Ley has called the movement's ideas simplistic and linked them to historical anti-masturbation campaigns, according to Wikipedia. [1] Wikipedia also reports that the American Psychiatric Association does not recognize pornography or sex addiction in the DSM-5 or DSM-5-TR and that the ICD-10 and ICD-11 do not list pornography addiction as a diagnosis. [1] The 2024 course survey and the 2025 review both characterize online men's-health content as frequently inaccurate. [3][5]

Wikipedia says NoFap has stated that researchers are prohibited from studying its community, and that in 2026 Rhodes filed a federal lawsuit against Aylo, UCLA, Taylor and Francis and scientists Nicole Prause and David Ley. [1] Wikipedia describes a related dispute in which Prause received damages from NoFap's legal counsel. [1] Supporters of the movement dispute the critics' characterizations.

The practice involves no substance. The IBTimes UK explainer says that for most healthy men abstinence is unlikely to cause serious harm, with temporary testicular discomfort and psychological effects such as irritability, anxiety and an obsessive focus on keeping a streak. [10] Researchers describe distress tied to relapse framing in rebooting forums, and the 2024 letter documents semen-loss anxiety. [6][7] Wikipedia says prolonged abstinence might worsen existing mental-health problems. [1]

timeline.event: A study reporting higher testosterone after seven days of abstinence is published; it is retracted in 2021. [1]
A study reports Dhat-like semen-loss symptoms among white Britons. [8]
Alexander Rhodes starts the NoFap community on Reddit after reading about the 2003 study. [1]
Within about two years of founding membership has more than tripled and Rhodes launches the off-Reddit forum NoFap.com. [1]
Rhodes leaves a job at Google to develop NoFap full time. [1]
The 2003 study is retracted; a critical narrative analysis of NoFap forum posts is published. [1][6]
A study of TikTok and Instagram finds semen retention among the least accurate and most viewed men's-health topics. [2][4]
Prause and Binnie publish a preregistered survey of reboot and NoFap participants. [1]
Studies of online ejaculation-training courses and of Dhat syndrome in semen-retention groups appear. [3][7]
Rhodes files a federal lawsuit naming Aylo, UCLA, Taylor and Francis, and researchers; a bibliometric analysis of masturbation research is published. [1][9]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and in wider retention culture, abstinence is presented as a self-improvement practice, and outside commentators treat it with skepticism. [11][12][13]

claims.claim: Abstaining from masturbation improves confidence and success in life.
claims.believers: Posters describe NoFap as a key to success and as an answer to insecurities about race or height. [11][12]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that the most prominent claimed benefits lack evidence, and researchers found commitment to abstinence maintained distress in forum members. [1][6]

claims.claim: Semen retention forces the body to make itself more attractive.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread argues retention redirects the body's resources toward attractiveness. [13]
claims.experts: No published study has tested semen retention for appearance, and a survey of online courses found health claims unsubstantiated. [3]

claims.believers: Proponents point to a 2003 study reporting a rise after seven days. [1]
claims.experts: That study was retracted in 2021, and an explainer reports any change is temporary and returns to baseline. [1][10]

claims.claim: Retained semen is a store of vital energy.
claims.believers: Followers cite Taoist jing and yogic brahmacharya as traditions teaching that semen holds vital energy. [10]
claims.experts: Fertility specialists quoted in coverage say unejaculated sperm is reabsorbed by the body and does not build up dangerously. [10]

claims.claim: Porn and frequent masturbation blunt dopamine and motivation, and a reboot reverses it.
claims.believers: This idea is associated with Gary Wilson and is widely repeated in rebooting communities. [1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports historian Brian Watson calling Wilson's work pseudoscience and notes pornography addiction is not a recognized diagnosis in DSM-5-TR or ICD-11. [1]

claims.claim: A long streak makes sexual function and fertility better.
claims.believers: Course marketing claims improved erectile function, premature ejaculation and sexual performance. [3]
claims.experts: Explainers report that a few days of abstinence may raise semen volume while longer abstinence may reduce motility and raise DNA fragmentation. [10]

claims.claim: Abstinence framing can itself cause distress.
claims.believers: Community members describe relapse and streak resets as setbacks to recover from. [6]
claims.experts: A 2021 analysis found abstinence framing maintained distress, and a 2024 letter describes semen-loss anxiety in these groups. [6][7]

claims.claim: Streaks are about discipline, not hormones.
claims.believers: Some members say the habit-tracking and time saved matter more than any physiological effect. [10]
claims.experts: The IBTimes UK explainer says reported benefits may come from related changes such as less pornography use, more exercise and stricter routines. [10]
